public_source_commits.subject: Implement Candidate04 weapon progression and physical upgrade machines
Exercise Last Word during machine stress profiles

final_text_audit.s2_content_binding_method: At curation, existing audited SHA-256 snapshots were compared with S2 Git text blobs. Exact bytes matched for 187 files; 98 differ only by CRLF/LF conversion. For 33 mixed-line-ending files, current bytes still match the recorded audit digest and normalize to the S2 blob. No binary asset was reread or rescanned for this binding.
final_text_audit.coverage: All current nonignored supported text extensions, including code, configuration, scripts, documentation, JSON and CSV. Checks cover credential-like tokens, secret assignments, personal home paths, machine-identity fields, private network addresses, UTF-8 decoding and common double-encoding artifacts. The detailed audit retains per-file hashes.

s2_delta_review.scope: Profile setup acquires Last Word through production controls, verifies actual upgraded combat and records the effective-upgrade CSV counter. No Content or other binary asset changes occur between S1 and S2.

fresh_checkout_lfs_integrity.scope: Integrity of final committed payloads, not a new privacy content scan.

scope_limits: The full ancestry/index/working-payload scan was recorded while HEAD was the public Candidate03 baseline and Candidate04 work was uncommitted: 873 nonignored working files. It is not represented as a post-S2 full binary rescan.

The earlier full scan inspected 29 public-ancestry commits, 768 historical/index Git blobs and 1,140 unique content payloads; referenced LFS objects were verified, compressed Blender content was expanded, and generated/private paths were screened. Its LFS totals cover outgoing versions and differ from final checkout counts.

The later 318-file text scan and explicit two-commit ancestry/delta review supplement that earlier scan. Final text snapshots are bound to S2 as described; no additional complete binary-metadata scan is claimed.

Heuristic scanning is not proof that every possible secret or private datum is absent. Binary release privacy, compressed cooked data, media inspection, archive contents and future documentation/evidence changes require their own coverage.
Private rollback refs, unrelated ignored files, raw diagnostics, host names and device identifiers are excluded from this public report.
